title: Contract stores and emits a map whose keys all read as "1"
pattern: An ScMap may hold keys of different types that print the same: u32 1, i32 1, u64 1, the string "1" and the symbol "1" are five distinct, correctly ordered keys on chain. Converting the map to a native object keyed by text collapses them. js-stellar-sdk's scValToNative silently kept one of them (#1789). This entry is real stellar-core output: a contract wrote the map to storage, returned it and emitted it in an event.

facts.says: The contract wrote a persistent entry keyed `collide` whose value is a 5-entry map with keys u32 1, i32 1, u64 1, string "1", symbol "1" (in core's order).
The event emitted by the call carries the same map with all 5 entries.
The return value is the same 5-entry map.
Each key maps to a different value (10, 20, 30, 40, 50), so a lossy conversion is detectable.

sdk_checks.says: Native projection of the event's map keeps all five entries or rejects the map; it never silently drops one.
sdk_checks.must: return 5 entries, or raise an error; returning fewer than 5 is a failure (js-stellar-sdk#1789)
